scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: An electric kettle boils water, then clicks off on its own. How does it know the water is boiling?

scenes.name: element
scenes.text: At the bottom is a heating element. Current flows through it and it gets very hot, heating the water.

scenes.name: steam
scenes.text: When water boils, steam rises and is guided through a small channel to the switch.

scenes.name: bimetal
scenes.text: There sits a bimetallic disc, two metals stuck together, that expand by different amounts when heated.

scenes.name: snap
scenes.text: The hot steam makes the disc suddenly snap into a new shape, pushing the switch and cutting the power.

scenes.name: dry
scenes.text: A second sensor under the base cuts power if the kettle is switched on empty.

scenes.name: fast
scenes.text: Since the heater sits right in the water, very little heat is wasted, which is why kettles boil so quickly.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Heat, steam, snap, off. Follow for more on how things really work.
